title: Special Circumstances: Jury May Not Consider Punishment

source.release: 2026 Criminal Jury Instructions (as adopted by the Judicial Council, February 2026)

body: In your deliberations, you may not consider or discuss penalty or punishment in any way when deciding whether a special circumstance, or any other charge, has been proved.

bench_notes.text: The court has a sua sponte duty to instruct the jury not to consider penalty or punishment when deciding on the special circumstances or other charges. (*People v. Robertson* (1982) 33 Cal.3d 21, 36 [188 Cal.Rptr. 77, 655 P.2d 279]; *People v. Holt* (1984) 37 Cal.3d 436, 458 [208 Cal.Rptr. 547, 690 P.2d 1207] [jury may not consider punishment in deciding on special circumstances].)

authority.text: • Duty to Instruct. *People v. Robertson* (1982) 33 Cal.3d 21, 36 [188 Cal.Rptr. 77, 655 P.2d 279].
